title: Sales/CS Feature Bundle Normalizer and Quick Econ Scan
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Build a lightweight, repeatable process and accompanying artifact that normalizes batches of incoming enterprise feature asks from Sales and Customer Success into canonical feature bundles, assigns a weighted priority score, and outputs a one-page initial economic and engineering scoping sketch. This ticket covers: (1) a normalization rubric (text-to-canonical mapping rules + synonyms), (2) a weighted scoring formula that blends account strategic value / ARR, customer urgency, cross-account demand, and rough engineering effort, and (3) an output template for PM/Eng quick-decide review and CS handback. The goal is to reduce friction in first-pass scoping and improve consistency for handoffs to Dedicated/Private product streams.
acceptance_criteria: Normalization rubric documented with at least 12 synonym rules and 5 example mappings
Scoring formula specified and validated on a test set of 80 historical asks with a sanity-check correlation to previous prioritizations
Deliverable: single-page 'Quick Econ & Scope' template populated by automation for 3 recent customer asks
Automation PoC (script) that ingests CSV from CS and emits canonical bundles and priority scores
Stakeholder alignment: Sales, CS, and two PMs have approved the rubric and scoring in review meeting
comments: 2026-03-02 — Kickoff: Met with Sales ops (Nate) and CS leads (Priya). Agreed painful parts: inconsistent ask wording, account context missing, and duplicate feature variants. Next: get sample CSV exports from top 30 accounts.

2026-03-04 — Initial rubric draft posted to Confluence: includes normalization buckets (Analytics, Routing, Security, Deployability) and a rule set for phrase collapsing (e.g., 'on-prem'|'VPC' -> 'private-deploy'). Asking ENG to review for edge cases around model-serving terms.

2026-03-06 — Eng review (@Ravi Patel): suggested adding 'compatibility constraints' flag for Dedicated/Private only features and recommended limiting free-text mapping to top 150 tokens to avoid noisy matches. Also raised potential privacy concern with direct ingestion of customer PII — added to security review queue.

2026-03-08 — PM sync: reduced engineer-side effort by defining three scoping tiers (Quick, Light, Deep) with default effort ranges. Decided to surface a 'confidence' score in the one-pager to indicate how much follow-up is required.

2026-03-09 — PoC script (Python) created that normalizes a 200-row CS dump and outputs 42 canonical bundles. Early results: consolidation rate ~22% (duplicates merged), top 5 bundles cover 47% of asks. Shared output CSV and example one-pagers in the drive link below.

2026-03-10 — Design feedback from Elena (Design): suggested an intake form change to capture 'expected timeline' and 'regulatory constraint' fields to improve scoring. Added to labels and intake form TODOs. Planning stakeholder demo on 2026-03-12.
notes: This ticket intentionally focuses on the 'first-pass' artifact and lightweight automation. Do not conflate with full productization of a customer portal. Next phase (if validated) will move normalization logic into Redwood Console intake flows and tie scoring to account economic signals from Revenue Ops.
next_steps: Run scoring formula on 80 additional asks and compute alignment metric vs historical prioritization (owner: Liam)
Prototype intake form change in CS tool and run A/B with 2 SDRs (owner: Elena)
Complete security review and sanitize PoC CSV ingestion to remove PII (owner: Ravi)
Demo one-pager output to Sales leadership on 2026-03-12 and capture sign-off criteria
